Output the delivered total, that ratio as a reduced fraction, and the lexicographically smallest path-flow tuple in input order.

title: Best position for a fixed display window
problem: Input an integer-coordinate board of width and height at most eight, a fixed axis-aligned window of integer width and height, and up to 12 weighted integer-coordinate points. Place the window with integer-coordinate lower-left corner wholly within the board. A point on its boundary counts as covered. Output the maximum sum of weights covered by one placement.

title: Fewest adjacent swaps to a palindrome
problem: Input a string of at most 12 characters over a–d. One move exchanges two neighboring characters. Output the minimum number of moves needed to obtain any palindrome, or -1 if no rearrangement of the characters is a palindrome.

title: Rearrange blocks through one empty slot
problem: Input a current array of at most 7 disk slots containing distinct named blocks and exactly one empty slot, plus a target permutation of the same entries. A move copies any block into the empty slot, leaving that block's former slot empty. Output the fewest moves needed to reach the target and, among shortest solutions, the lexicographically smallest sequence of source-slot indices.

title: Remove Joins Without Changing Projected Rows
problem: Input gives up to 4 named tables of at most 5 explicit rows each, a scan cost per table, equality join edges, and a nonempty list of projected columns. Evaluate joins with bag semantics: every compatible row combination contributes one projected tuple. Among connected table subsets containing every projected column's table, find one whose projected-output multiset equals that of the full join. Output its minimum total scan cost and table names, breaking ties by the sorted name list.

title: Partition a loop into scalar and vector operations
problem: Input gives N consecutive iterations, with 1 ≤ N ≤ 20, a starting address A, and positive costs for one scalar operation and for vector operations of widths 2 and 4. Partition the iterations, in order, into nonoverlapping blocks of those widths. A vector block of width w is allowed only when the address of its first iteration, A plus its zero-based iteration index, is divisible by w. Output the minimum total cost.

title: Arc-consistent domains
problem: Input at most eight finite-domain variables, each with at most four values, and binary constraints given as lists of allowed value pairs. A complete satisfying assignment is supplied. Repeatedly remove any value lacking a compatible remaining value across some incident constraint. Output the final domain of each variable in its original value order.

title: Parenthesize a rounded rational sum
problem: Input is 2 to 7 rational numbers with numerators in [-10,10] and positive denominators at most 10, plus a positive grid denominator D at most 10. Preserve input order and choose a full binary parenthesization. At each internal node, add its two child values and round the sum down to the nearest multiple of 1/D; leaves retain their exact input values. Minimize the final absolute error relative to the exact sum of all leaves. Output the exact rational error and the optimal parenthesization, breaking ties by its lexicographic fully parenthesized string using zero-based leaf indices.

title: Shortest nonzero parity solution
problem: Input an r-by-n binary matrix H, with 1≤r≤4 and 1≤n≤6. Find a nonzero binary vector x satisfying Hx=0 modulo 2. Output its minimum possible Hamming weight and, among vectors of that weight, the lexicographically smallest x. Output NONE if no nonzero solution exists.

title: Find the fewest FIFO output lanes
problem: Input is a target permutation p of 1..n, with n ≤ 9. First assign each value of 1,2,...,n, in that order, to one of k FIFO lanes; no values may be removed during this phase. Then repeatedly remove a front value from any lane to produce p. Output the smallest k that permits p.

title: Aim a solar tracker powered by its own battery
problem: Given T≤7, two panel orientations, an initial orientation, battery capacity C≤5, initial charge, inverter export limit L≤3, and an integer generation value for each orientation and slot, maximize total exported energy. At each slot's start the tracker may stay or switch orientation; switching immediately consumes one stored battery unit and is forbidden if none is available. The panel then generates its stated energy. Choose an integer export up to L, store any remaining energy up to C, and curtail any excess. Output the maximum total export.

title: Fewest active switch slots
problem: Input: at most 7 packets over at most 7 slots. Each packet has an input port, output port, release slot, and deadline slot. In a slot, transmitted packets must use distinct input ports and distinct output ports; a packet can be sent in any one slot from its release through its deadline. Output the minimum number of slots containing at least one transmission that delivers every packet, or -1 if impossible.

title: Shape a small two-dimensional point index
problem: Input: up to 6 distinct integer-coordinate points and weighted axis-aligned rectangle queries. Build a binary tree with one point per leaf. Each internal node partitions its points by an x- or y-coordinate threshold between consecutive distinct values, leaving both children nonempty. A query loads the root, then loads a child exactly when that child's point bounding box intersects the rectangle; each load costs 1. Output the minimum weighted number of loads over all valid tree shapes.

title: Recover an exact repeating tile
problem: Input an at-most-8×8 symbol grid. Find tile dimensions h and w that divide the grid height and width and whose top-left h×w tile exactly reproduces the grid by repetition. Output dimensions with minimum area, breaking ties by smaller h then smaller w, and output the tile itself.

title: Represent a matrix by sparse differences
problem: Input an integer matrix at most 5 by 5 and a list of inclusive rectangular sum queries. Define D[i,j] = A[i,j] - A[i-1,j] - A[i,j-1] + A[i-1,j-1], treating out-of-bounds entries as zero. Output the nonzero (row, column, value) entries of D in row-major order and the sum of A over each query rectangle. The difference entries must exactly reconstruct A by two-dimensional prefix summation.

title: Shortest failing subsequence
problem: Input a total deterministic machine with at most 6 states and 3 ordered input symbols, a start state, a set of failure states, and an input sequence of length at most 16 whose final state is a failure state. Delete any positions while retaining the order of the remaining symbols. Output the lexicographically smallest list of retained zero-based positions among all shortest subsequences whose final state is a failure state; the empty list is allowed.

title: Paint a small board by strokes
problem: Input gives initial and target color grids of at most 3 by 3 cells using at most three colors, plus a stroke sequence reaching the target. One stroke chooses a row or column and overwrites every cell in it with one chosen color. Output the minimum number of strokes needed to produce the target grid.
